proper_power_obstruction.consequence: 3 is not an a-th power in positive integers for any a>=2

impact.beal_frontier_use: This removes every canonical or noncanonical Beal signature whose exponents can be grouped as a multiple of 2 at least 4, a multiple of 3, and a multiple of 10, with the indicated power constraints on the bases.
impact.family: an infinite three-parameter family, including all six exponent permutations

nonclaim: The finite replay verifies the substitutions, signs, equations, primitivity and the proper-power obstruction. Completeness of Brown's 12-solution list and Dahmen's n=5 no-solution theorem are imported peer-reviewed mathematical inputs. This does not prove the full Beal conjecture.

right_exponent_10c.elimination: the complete Brown list contains no row with all three coordinates positive

right_exponent_2a.elimination: the only compatible row is (3,-2,1), which would force C^a=3 and is impossible for a>=2

right_exponent_3b.elimination: Dahmen's theorem for n=5 gives no nonzero coprime solution of x^2+y^(2n)=z^3

primitivity_bridge: Raising pairwise-coprime positive bases to positive powers preserves pairwise coprimality, so every substitution satisfies the hypotheses of the imported primitive/coprime source theorem.

theorem.permutation_coverage: The three choices of right-hand exponent are recorded explicitly; swapping the two positive summands covers all six permutations.
theorem.statement: For every a>=2 and b,c>=1, no pairwise-coprime positive integers solve any coefficient-one generalized Fermat equation whose exponent multiset is {2a,3b,10c}.
